reference_answer: For the September 11 Nx socket advisory GHSA-w3vv-58gj-gw77, product management UI's pinned nx/@nx/angular 22.5.3 is in the affected >=14.6 <22.7.9 range. Financial HQ UI's 23.2.1 is beyond the affected 23.0 <23.1.2 range. The attack needs another local user on the same host while an Nx daemon/plugin worker is running, so prioritize shared CI/build hosts and upgrade product management's Nx packages together to at least 22.7.9; reset old daemon state on shared hosts. The July remote-cache Zip-Slip advisory is another plausible 'recent Nx issue': product management 22.5.3 is in its affected version range, financial 23.2.1 is not; exposure requires self-hosted remote cache, which is not evident from the tracked config. Verify CI environment and cache packages before assessing exploitability; upgrade and migrate deprecated cache packages if used.
